audit.report: A replayable batch job (inventory_reconcile, pid 336116) idled in an open transaction for over 4 seconds, holding locks that blocked 12 sessions and crashed checkout success to 7% with $17,037/min revenue at risk. The Database Guardian proposed terminating the blocker; the Continuity Guardian requested a change-calendar check (Invariant I2), which returned clean. After the second round, both guardians agreed to terminate. The executor killed the session and the verifier confirmed full recovery: zero lock waits and 100% checkout success over 10 seconds.
audit.root_cause: The inventory_reconcile batch worker (pid 336116) idled in an open transaction holding locks, blocking checkout sessions and violating the 60-second degradation tolerance.
lessons: Add a statement_timeout or idle_in_transaction_session_timeout to the batch_replayable_inventory role so inventory_reconcile cannot idle in transaction and hold locks.
Pre-load the change-calendar status for inventory_reconcile into the runbook so the Continuity Guardian can approve termination in round 1 without a probe.
Instrument inventory_reconcile to emit a heartbeat or checkpoint metric; if it stalls >30s, alert on-call before it becomes a blocker.
audit.negotiation_critique: The Database Guardian correctly identified the blocker and quantified the revenue impact in round 1. The Continuity Guardian properly enforced Invariant I2 (change-calendar check) but the required probe added a full round; no evidence was missed and neither guardian wasted a round.
follow_ups: Apply idle_in_transaction_session_timeout to the batch_worker role used by inventory_reconcile.
Update the inventory_reconcile runbook with the change-calendar query and a pre-approved termination playbook.
Add a stall alert on inventory_reconcile checkpoint lag >30s.

proposal.rationale: The root blocker is pid 336116 (batch_worker/batch_replayable_inventory) idle in transaction for 4.1s with last statement SELECT 1 [DB-1]. This session holds locks blocking 1 session and contributing to 12 total waiting sessions. Checkout is degraded at 92% success (4 timeouts in 15s) [TEL-1] and 83% over 10s vs 95% SLO with $3,172/min revenue at risk [BIZ-1]. Business tolerates at most 60s degraded checkout [BIZ-1]. The blocker's application name 'batch_replayable_inventory' suggests replayable workload. Need registry/tradeoff to confirm interrupt policy and cost, and protected_settlements to ensure no in-flight payments blocked.
proposal.expected_effect: Terminating pid 336116 releases its locks, unblocking the 1 directly blocked session and reducing lock contention for checkout. Checkout success rate should recover toward SLO within seconds. Revenue at risk ($3,172/min) stops accruing once checkout recovers.
proposal.risk_assessment: If batch_replayable_inventory is not actually replayable or has side effects, termination could cause data inconsistency or require manual replay. If protected settlements are blocked by this session, termination could disrupt payment processing. Need registry and tradeoff to quantify interrupt cost vs wait cost.
